subject: RFP: Model provenance, licensing compatibility, and version-change controls
messages:
From: Alejandra Gomez <agomez@bluelake.com>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.inference>
Cc: Tom Hsu <thsu@bluelake.com>, DLG Legal <legal@bluelake.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: RFP: Model provenance & licensing controls

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for taking the time to engage on our RFP. BlueLake is evaluating vendors for a platform that can serve mixed open and proprietary models while giving us strict control over licensing compatibility, model origin metadata, and predictable behavior for pinned versions. A few specific asks we want covered in the RFI response: 

- How you represent model provenance (training data lineage, third-party model attribution, SBOM-equivalent artifacts).
- Policy and tooling for version pinning and how long pinned artifacts are guaranteed to be available.
- Mechanisms for notifying customers of model updates, deprecations, and emergency security patches.
- How you handle open-model license compatibility (commercial use, attribution, share-alike requirements) and what attestations you provide.
- Exportable audit logs and evidence for SOC2 / procurement review.

Could you send an RFI response and any sample artifacts we can include in our procurement pack by EOD tomorrow (Apr 12)? Our legal team will likely have follow-ups.

Best,
Alejandra
Procurement Lead
BlueLake Systems

Subject: Re: RFP: Model provenance & licensing controls

Alejandra —

Thanks for the clear list. Attached is our RFI package that addresses each bullet (Redwood_RFI_Model_Catalog_Answers.pdf) and a machine-readable provenance export (model-provenance-export-20270411.jsonl) for a sample open model in our catalog. High-level summary below: 

1) Provenance: We attach model-level provenance metadata (architecture, upstream model id, training-corpora tags, credentialed contributor list) and an SBOM-style artifact that lists third-party components used in model compilation. Artifacts are queryable via API and exportable as JSONL for auditors.

2) Version pinning: Customers may pin any published model revision. Pin guarantees: pinned revisions are retained on the serving tier for a minimum of 12 months from pin date or until the customer explicitly unpins; we offer a paid archival retention option beyond 12 months. Pins include a fingerprint (SHA-256 of the model artifact) and a static config snapshot.

3) Update notifications & change control: We provide a staged notification policy — normal updates: 90-day advance notice via email + console obsolescence banner; deprecation window: 90-day; emergency security patches: immediate notification + emergency patch stream (no automatic migration of pinned revisions). We also publish a changelog and maintain an immutable timeline per model id.

4) License compatibility: Our model catalog stores license metadata per artifact (SPDX id), plus a compatibility matrix that surfaces models with restrictive clauses (e.g., AGPL-style share-alike). For models with ambiguous licensing, we surface a legal-risk flag and require explicit acceptance before provisioning at scale. We provide a signed attestation for catalog entries and can include a per-deal license addendum when needed.

5) Audit evidence: We include exportable audit logs (API access, model selection, pin/unpin events) and SOC2 artifact summaries. See attached SOC2-evidence-summary.zip for typical items we share with procurement/legal.

I'll follow up with a short note answering the two points I expect legal to care most about (pin lifetime & update rollback semantics). Happy to set a 30-minute call tomorrow with our product/legal if helpful.

Regards,
Sofia Ivanova

Subject: Re: RFP: Model provenance & licensing controls

Sofia —

Thanks for the quick package; the artifacts look good at a glance. Two follow-ups from DLG Legal: 

A) On pinned revisions: can you confirm whether pinned revisions are eligible for security patches (i.e., do you ever backport security fixes into a pinned artifact or are patches always delivered as a separate patched artifact)? Legal prefers a clear statement that pinned artifacts are immutable and that security fixes are provided as separate artifacts with migration guidance.

B) On notification timing: 90 days is reasonable for planned updates. For cloud customers with regulatory constraints, would you commit to a longer pinned-availability window (e.g., 24 months) under a contractual addendum? If so, what are the commercial terms (baseline vs addendum)?

If you can reply with short, contractual-style statements we can pass to procurement/legal, that would help us move to the next stage.

Thanks,
Tom
BlueLake Systems

Subject: Fwd: RFP: Model provenance & licensing controls — legal follow-ups (need short contractual wording)

Team —

DLG Legal at BlueLake asked two precise things: immutability/patching behavior for pinned revisions, and whether we can offer a 24-month retention under contract (and on what terms). Draft below that I'd like to send back to them; please confirm language or edits by EOD today. We'll attach the evidence bundle and add a line about addendum pricing.

DRAFT CONTRACTUAL RESPONSES (please comment):

1) Pinned Artifact Immutability and Security Patches — Contractual Statement (draft):
"Pinned model revisions are treated as immutable artifacts. Redwood will not modify the binary content of a pinned revision. In the event of a security vulnerability affecting a pinned revision, Redwood will: (a) publish a security advisory, (b) create a patched successor revision and make migration guidance available, and (c) provide a temporary emergency patch stream as a separate artifact if requested under the emergency support terms in the contract. Customers who elect to remain on a pinned revision acknowledge they are not auto-migrated to patched content and are responsible for scheduled migration planning."

2) Extended Retention for Pinned Artifacts — Contractual Statement (draft):
"Redwood guarantees retention of customer-pinned revisions for a minimum of twelve (12) months from pin date as part of the baseline service. Customers may purchase extended retention (up to twenty-four (24) months) via a contractual addendum. Extended retention fees are negotiated per-deal and depend on archival storage class and access SLA; typical addendum pricing is 15% of the annual Dedicated capacity commitment for the first additional year of retention. Redwood will provide technical documentation and an export mechanism for archived artifacts during the extended retention period."

Please add any legal or commercial flags. Karthik — pricing tweak? Neha — ok for product/legal? Priyom — any CS notes on migration guidance?

Thanks,
Sofia

Alejandra / Tom / DLG Legal —

Per Tom's asks, please find concise contractual-style responses below and the evidence bundle attached. If this meets your needs, we can incorporate these statements into an NDA/Addendum.

1) Pinned Artifact Immutability and Security Patches (contractual wording):
"Pinned model revisions are immutable. Redwood will not alter the binary contents of a pinned revision. If a security vulnerability is discovered that affects a pinned revision, Redwood will (i) publish a security advisory to the customer and on the Console, (ii) produce a patched successor revision with migration guidance, and (iii) upon customer request and per the emergency support terms, provide an emergency patch stream as a separate artifact. Customers remain in control of migration timing for pinned revisions and are not auto-migrated."

2) Extended Retention for Pinned Artifacts (contractual wording):
"Baseline service includes a 12-month retention guarantee for customer-pinned revisions. Extended retention (up to 24 months) is available through a contractual addendum. Extended retention fees are negotiated per-deal; as an indicative example, Redwood typically prices the first additional 12 months of retention at ~15% of the customer's annual Dedicated capacity commitment. All archived artifacts remain accessible via the Redwood API with documented export procedures."

3) Additional clarifications: license compatibility is surfaced via SPDX tags and a legal-risk flag in the Console; we provide a signed attestation for catalog entries on request; audit logs and SOC2 summary are attached.

Next steps: If you want, we can: (a) add these statements into your NDA/addendum draft, (b) set a 30-minute call with our product counsel (Neha) and Karthik (commercial lead) to finalize commercial terms, or (c) send a DocuSign-ready addendum template.

I can make time tomorrow morning for a quick call if helpful.

Regards,
